    Jacques-Louis David/On view
    What are the characteristics of Jacques-Louis David paintings?
    Jacques-Louis David developed a painting style of harmonious realism and sharp clarity, which came to be known as neoclassicism. Historians contrast the neoclassical style of Jacques-Louis David art against the highly decorative style of rococo that dominated French painting in the 18th century.

    What was Jacques-Louis David known for?
    Jacques-Louis David was the leading painter in France of the Neo-classical movement. He became a member of the Academy in 1783, winning fame in the 1780s with a series of paintings, including 'The Oath of the Horatii' (Paris, Louvre, 1785), notable for their austerity of design and theme.

    About

    Description

    Jacques-Louis David was a French painter in the Neoclassical style, considered to be the preeminent painter of the era. Wikipedia
    Born: August 30, 1748, Paris, France
    Died: December 29, 1825 (age 77 years), Brussels, Belgium
    Period: Neoclassicism
    Influenced by: Nicolas Poussin, François Boucher, Valentin de Boulogne
    Spouse: Charlotte David (m. 1796–1825), Charlotte David (m. 1782–1793)
    Children: Pauline Jeanne David, Laure Émilie Félicité David, Eugène David, Jules David
    Parents: Louis-Maurice, Marie-Geneviève Buron
